questions.question: If the state government ___ the requisition to the High Court by Friday, the examination notification will be issued next month.
questions.explanation: Result clause 'will be issued' First Conditional form mein hai. Subordinate conditional if-clause mein future time hone par bhi 'will' nahi lagta; wahan Simple Present 'submits' (B) lagega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: 'If + Simple Present (V1/V_s/es), will + V1'. If-clause rejects future auxiliary 'will'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the judicial clerk had the updated procedural manual on his desk, he ___ the query without consulting the superintendent.
questions.explanation: If-clause Simple Past verb 'had' (possession) use kar raha hai jo present imaginary condition express karta hai. Second Conditional formula ke hisaab se result clause mein 'would + V1' lagta hai: 'would resolve' (B).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Present hypothetical state (Simple Past V2) requires 'would + V1' in the result clause.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If I ___ the counsel for the defense, I would object to the admission of this unverified electronic record.
questions.explanation: Contrary-to-fact hypothetical condition mein formal English aur competitive exams mein sabhi persons ke sath subjunctive 'were' (C) use hota hai. 'Was' (B) informal speech tak seemit hai aur exam standard par incorrect mana jata hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Formal subjunctive concord requires 'were' for all persons in hypothetical conditionals.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the forensic expert had tested the handwriting samples rigorously, the trial court ___ the forged promissory note.
questions.explanation: If-clause Past Perfect ('had tested') mein hai jo beete huye past unfulfilled action ko express karta hai. Third Conditional formula: 'If + had + V3, would have + V3'. Result clause mein 'would have detected' (B) lagega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Unreal past conditions require 'would have + V3' in the consequential clause.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If mercury ___ heated, it expands uniformly at a measurable rate.
questions.explanation: Mercury ka heat hone par expand hona ek universal physical law hai. Zero Conditional formula: Simple Present + Simple Present. Passive voice mein singular noun 'mercury' ke sath Simple Present auxiliary 'is' (A) aayega ('is heated').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Permanent physical processes take Simple Present in both condition and result clauses.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: ___ the administrative registrar reviewed the biometric attendance records, the unauthorized absenteeism would have been checked.
questions.explanation: Main verb V3 'reviewed' hai aur result clause 'would have been checked' hai. Ye Third Conditional ki formal inverted form hai: 'Had + Subject + V3 ..., would have + V3'. Isliye 'Had' (C) sahi answer hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: 'Had + Subject + V3 ..., would have + V3' forms formal Type 3 inversion.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: Were the High Court committee ___ the promotion rules, several experienced assistants would benefit immediately.
questions.explanation: Jab action verb ko Type 2 conditional mein 'Were' ke sath invert karte hain, toh structure 'Were + Subject + to + V1' follow hota hai: 'to amend' (B). Result clause 'would benefit' is hypothetical alignment ko confirm karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Action verb inversion with Were requires 'Were + Subject + to + V1'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: ___ you notice any discrepancy in the provisional answer key, submit your formal objection within three days.
questions.explanation: Base verb V1 'notice' aur result clause imperative instruction 'submit' formal Type 1 inversion ko indicate karte hain. Structure: 'Should + Subject + V1 ..., Imperative'. Isliye 'Should' (A) sahi option hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: 'Should + Subject + V1' introduces formal contingency in conditional structures.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.subtopic: Error Identification: Would Have in If-Clause
questions.question:
Identify the incorrect part of the sentence:

'If the trial judge (A) / would have examined the alibi witness, (B) / the verdict would have been (C) / completely different. (D)'

options.text: would have examined the alibi witness,

questions.explanation: Part B grammatically incorrect hai. Subordinate conditional if-clause ke andar 'would have' ka use prohibited hai. Yahan Past Perfect 'had examined' hona chahiye: 'If the trial judge had examined the alibi witness...'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule PIT-01: 'Would have' is strictly prohibited inside the if-clause. Use 'had + V3'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: Unless the appellant ___ the requisite court fees within the stipulated period, the memorandum of appeal will be rejected.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' clause inherently negative hota hai, isliye iske andar 'does not' (A) lagane se double negative banta hai. Future 'will' (C) bhi nahi lag sakta. Isliye 3rd person singular subject 'the appellant' ke sath Simple Present affirmative 'deposits' (B) correct answer hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & PIT-04: 'Unless' clause must be affirmative in form and take Simple Present for future conditions.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the computer programmer had patched the server kernel last week, the judicial portal ___ stable today.
questions.explanation: Sentence Mixed Conditional represent karta hai: Condition past time ki hai ('had patched last week'), lekin result present time ka state hai ('today'). Result clause mein present hypothetical state ke liye 'would be' (B) aayega, 'would have been' (A) nahi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Mixed Conditional (Past Unreal Condition ➔ Present Result): 'If + had + V3, would + V1 (today/now)'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: The candidate will be granted compensatory typing time, provided that he ___ a valid medical board disability certificate.
questions.explanation: 'Provided that' conditional clause banata hai. First Conditional framework ke mutabiq condition clause mein future event ke liye Simple Present 'produces' (B) lagta hai, 'will produce' (A) nahi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Clauses introduced by 'provided that' take Simple Present for future conditions.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: Choose the sentence that displays FLAWLESS grammatical word order:

options.text: Had not the police officer secured the crime scene, the fingerprints would have been lost.
Had the police officer not secured the crime scene, the fingerprints would have been lost.
Did the police officer not secured the crime scene, the fingerprints would have been lost.
Were not the police officer securing the crime scene, the fingerprints would have been lost.

questions.explanation: Option B standard formal negative inversion ka exact order hai: 'Had + Subject (the police officer) + not + V3 (secured)'. Option A mein 'Had not the police officer' word order error hai. Option C auxiliary 'Did' ke sath V3 'secured' galat use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule PIT-05: Inverted negative conditional syntax requires: 'Had + Subject + not + V3'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If the applicant had reached the examination center fifteen minutes earlier, he ___ the verification process on time.
questions.explanation: If-clause Past Perfect ('had reached') mein past unfulfilled condition dikhata hai. Result clause mein past unreal ability ko express karne ke liye 'could have + V3' ('could have completed') (B) lagega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Third Conditional expressing counterfactual past ability takes 'could have + V3'.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03

questions.question: If you detect any unauthorized login attempt on the court server, ___ the chief information security officer at once.
questions.explanation: Condition clause Simple Present ('detect') mein future contingency batata hai. Result clause direct administrative command/instruction hai, jiske liye imperative base verb V1 'alert' (B) use hoti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: First Conditional instructions and orders use base imperative verbs in the result clause.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L03
